title: Food and ordering
can: Order in a bar, get through the menú del día, mention allergies and ask for the bill.
doneText: You can now order like a local, from a caña at the bar to three courses of the menú del día.

discover.intro: Here are six ways to order. Look closely at the little word before each thing.

groups.label: With una
lines: Can I have a small beer?

discover.question: Why un in blue and una in orange?
options: It depends on the word: most words ending in -o take un, most ending in -a take una.
Una is more polite than un.
Un is for drinks and una is for food.
discover.nudge: Not quite. There are drinks and food in both colours. Look at how each word ends.
discover.reveal: Every noun in Spanish is masculine or feminine. Most -o words are masculine (un, el) and most -a words are feminine (una, la). For anything else, like café, learn the word together with its article.

learn.title: The little words
learn.sub: Tap any row to hear it

blocks.text: Plurals: add -s after a vowel (cañas, cafés) and -es after a consonant (raciones, panes).

In Spanish bars, ¿Me pones…? (literally "will you put me…?") is the everyday way to order, and waiters often say tú to customers. The menú del día is a set lunch: a first course, a main, a dessert, bread and a drink for one price.

blocks.title: La comida: lunch, or food
a: La comida es a las dos.
blocks.note: Es says when lunch is. Está says how the food tastes right now. In Spain, la comida is also the big midday meal.

blocks.text: Allergies use ser, because they are a characteristic: soy alérgic{o} a los frutos secos. With the noun it is tener: tengo alergia a los frutos secos.

write.title: Say it in your own words
write.task: Order the menú del día: choose a first course, a main and a dessert, then ask for the bill.
write.starter: Para mí, el menú del día. De primero…
write.model: Para mí, el menú del día. De primero, gazpacho. De segundo, la merluza. De postre, flan. ¿Me traes la cuenta, por favor?
checklist: Each course starts with de primero, de segundo or de postre
Dishes keep their el or la
Por favor or ¿Me traes…? for the bill

boss.title: Menú del día in a Madrid bar
boss.persona: You are Pepe, a chatty waiter in a busy bar in Madrid serving the menú del día at lunchtime. Use tú. Talk about dishes, drinks, desserts, allergies and the bill.

turns.en: Hi! What can I get you?
choices: El menú del día, por favor.
La menú del día, por favor.
Menú is masculine: el menú.
Estoy el menú del día.
Estoy means "I am". To order, name the thing and add por favor.

turns.npc: De primero hay gazpacho o ensalada mixta. ¿Qué te apetece?
turns.en: For starters there's gazpacho or mixed salad. What do you fancy?
choices: De primero, gazpacho.
De postre, gazpacho.
Postre is dessert. For the first course: de primero.
Primero de gazpacho.
The order is de primero, then the dish.

turns.npc: ¿Y de segundo? Hay pollo asado o merluza a la plancha.
turns.en: And for the main? There's roast chicken or grilled hake.
choices: De segundo, la merluza.
De segundo, el merluza.
Merluza ends in -a: la merluza.
De segundo, los merluza.
Los is plural and masculine. One hake: la merluza.

turns.en: Very good. Do you have any allergies?
choices: Sí, soy alérgic{o} a los frutos secos.
Sí, estoy alérgic{o} a los frutos secos.
An allergy is a characteristic: soy alérgico or alérgica.
Sí, tengo alérgic{o} a los frutos secos.
Tener needs the noun: tengo alergia a… With alérgico or alérgica, use soy.

boss.closing: Perfecto, sin frutos secos. Ahora te traigo el pan.
boss.closingEn: Perfect, no nuts. I'll bring you the bread now.
boss.chatOpeningEn: And to drink? Water, wine, a small beer…?
